items.title: The Fifth Element
items.line: Luc Besson's The Fifth Element opened in France on 7 May 1997 and opened Cannes. Jean Paul Gaultier did the costumes, and it grossed over $263 million.

items.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
items.line: In New York, 3 to 11 May 1997, IBM's Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5. He resigned game 6 after 19 moves and had already accused IBM of cheating.

items.title: Death of Princess Diana
items.line: Diana died in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris on 31 August 1997. An estimated 31.5 million people in Britain watched the Westminster Abbey funeral on 6 September.

items.title: Titanic
items.line: Titanic opened in the US on 19 December 1997. It cost $200 million, ran 195 minutes, won 11 Oscars from 14 nominations and has grossed about $2.26 billion over its releases.

items.title: Teletubbies
items.line: Teletubbies began on BBC2 on 31 March 1997, filmed on a Warwickshire farm. Their Eh-oh single reached number one in December and stayed in the UK Top 75 for 32 weeks.

items.title: Gran Turismo
items.line: Gran Turismo reached Japan on 23 December 1997 with 140 cars and 11 tracks. Kazunori Yamauchi directed it, and it became the best-selling PlayStation game at about 10.85 million.

items.title: Harry Potter
items.line: Bloomsbury published Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone on 26 June 1997. The first print run was 500 hardbacks, 300 of them for libraries, and Rowling's advance was £2,500.
